St. Pete Gag Grouper: Planning for September 2026

A short season makes it tempting to chase every forecast. Choose a trip you can finish safely, with the right rules and release gear already sorted.

By Catch 'N Bake · 4 minute read
Rules checked September 14, 2026. Check linked agencies for changes before fishing.

In this articleCheck the September 2026 gag seasonWrite the fishing area into the planA public reef coordinate is a starting pointSet up for the fish you will releaseChoose the return window before the first dropKeep the catch useful after the photo

Check the September 2026 gag season

September leaves a short window to keep Gulf gag grouper in 2026. For a trip from St. Pete, work backward from your return route: the pass you will use, the water you will cross, and how much time you can spend fishing. Then choose reef locations that fit.

2026 season check · September 14

FWC lists Gulf gag harvest as open September 1 through 30, 2026. NOAA lists the federal Gulf closure at 12:01 a.m. local time on October 1. Check both the FWC grouper rules and the NOAA season bulletin before your trip.

Old articles still circulate with different dates. The year matters, and so does the fishery. An Atlantic gag announcement does not describe the Gulf trip you are planning from St. Pete.

Write the fishing area into the plan

“Leaving from St. Pete” identifies the departure point. It does not identify the rules at the place you drop a bait. Plot the intended fishing area and establish whether you will fish state or federal waters before you leave. Check the regulations that apply to the vessel as well as the fish.

For Gulf gag, FWC lists a 24 inch total length minimum and two fish per person within the four grouper aggregate. Charter captain and crew have a zero gag bag limit. Those numbers belong beside the current season and applicable rules, not on a disconnected screenshot in your camera roll.

If you book a charter, ask what waters the captain expects to fish, what happens if weather changes the plan, and which species are realistic alternatives. Ask before paying whether a shortened or changed trip affects the booking. A gag target is not a promise of a gag catch.

A public reef coordinate is a starting point

Pinellas County's artificial reef map gives you a public source for reef locations. Use it to build a shortlist that fits your boat, range, and forecast. It does not tell you which reef holds keeper gag today.

On that shortlist, compare the whole route rather than distance from the ramp alone. Include the run through the pass, the return direction, and a fallback you can reach without extending the day. Leave shipping channels clear and give other boats room to fish.

When you arrive, take time to understand your position relative to the structure and current. Watch the line angle and whether you can maintain controlled contact with the bottom. If the boat cannot hold a workable position, dropping more bait is not a substitute for fixing the setup.

Record the depth and presentation you actually fished. A saved reef name without those details can turn a productive trip into a mystery when you return.

Set up for the fish you will release

A measuring tool, dehooker, and a ready release setup deserve space beside the bait. They are part of the trip even if you hope to put a legal gag on ice.

FWC's Gulf reef fish gear rules cover circle hooks when using natural bait, dehooking equipment, and a descending device or venting tool rigged and ready. The hook requirements differ in detail between state and federal waters. Read the matching section before rigging.

Learn the release tool before you need it. Keep the instructions with the equipment and practice the setup ashore. FWC's barotrauma guidance explains why a fish brought up from depth may need help returning. A tool still sealed in its packaging will slow that decision down.

Choose the return window before the first drop

Check the marine forecast for your planned route, not just the weather app's city forecast. The National Weather Service Tampa Bay office provides forecasts, radar, and warnings. Recheck before departure and while you have a reliable connection.

Give somebody ashore your plan. Agree on the return time with the people on board. If one more stop uses the margin you set aside for a slower ride home, skip it. You can change the fishing plan without turning the day into a failed trip.

Keep the catch useful after the photo

Once you confirm a fish is legal to retain, keep it cold and follow the applicable landing requirements. Decide where cleaning will happen before returning with a cooler to manage.

Our gag grouper taste and cooking guide covers fillet preparation and meal ideas. For the journal, save the depth, rig, bait, and whether the fish came from the first presentation or after a change. Those notes can make next September's planning more specific than “try that reef again.”

Keep the details for your next trip.
